procedure.description: application of skin substitute graft to the foot, first 25 square centimeters, diabetic foot ulcer

denial.carcText: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
denial.text: Silverline Medicare Advantage denied the claim for CPT 15271 (application of skin substitute graft to the foot, first 25 square centimeters, diabetic foot ulcer) with date of service 2026-02-13. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: Documentation does not meet coverage criteria for cellular and tissue-based products for wounds.

criteria.text: Full-thickness diabetic foot ulcer, Wagner grade 1 or 2, present for at least 4 weeks, without exposed bone or tendon, active infection, or osteomyelitis.

At least 4 weeks of standard wound care with documented serial measurements showing less than 50 percent reduction in wound area: sharp debridement, offloading, moist wound dressings, infection control, and glycemic management.
Adequate arterial perfusion documented: ankle-brachial index of 0.7 or greater, toe pressure of 40 mmHg or greater, or transcutaneous oxygen pressure of 30 mmHg or greater.
Hemoglobin A1c of 12 percent or less, an offloading device in place, and tobacco cessation counseling where applicable.

chart.text: Mole on the left forearm that her spouse noticed. About 5 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.

Twisted the left ankle stepping off a curb 4 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.
From the referring physician: please evaluate and treat as you see fit. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.
Blood pressure check. 131 over 89 today, 143 over 87 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 20 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 6 weeks.
Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.

Knee pain going down stairs, left side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 13 and 19. No ocular pathology noted.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 5 years.

Here with a cough and congestion for 5 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if she gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.

73 year old woman with type 2 diabetes for 18 years and peripheral neuropathy, new to the wound center, referred by podiatry. Did not notice the ulcer until her spouse saw blood on the sock. Her history otherwise: mild asthma, albuterol maybe twice a year, seasonal allergies, osteoarthritis of the hands. Allergies: codeine makes her sick. Quit smoking 10 years ago, no alcohol, stays home with the kids. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Plantar left forefoot ulcer under the first metatarsal head, present 6 weeks, 3.2 by 2.0 centimeters and 0.3 deep, full thickness into subcutaneous tissue, does not probe to bone, no exposed tendon, Wagner grade 2. No cellulitis, no drainage, no odor. Offloading boot dispensed today, fitted, she agrees to wear it for all weight bearing. Nonsmoker.
Hemoglobin A1c 8.8 percent. Creatinine 1.5. Albumin 3.8.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 40. Approved 90 days. She mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.
Mammogram report forwarded for the record. Bilateral screening, BI-RADS 1, negative, routine screening in one year.
Patient called about a tick bite on the scalp after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.
Left foot three views: no osteomyelitis, no soft tissue gas, no foreign body. Neuropathic changes at the midfoot.
Week 1 of standard care. Sharp debridement to healthy bleeding tissue, collagen dressing, offloading boot worn per patient. 3.2 by 2.0.
Arterial studies. Ankle-brachial index left 0.96, right 1.06, triphasic waveforms, left toe pressure 61 mmHg. Adequate perfusion for healing.
Work note requested for a sick day last Thursday. Faxed to the employer.
A1c came back 6.0. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. She is motivated.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.
Week 2. Sharp debridement, collagen dressing. 3.1 by 2.0. Boot compliance good.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the left for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.
Week 3. Sharp debridement, collagen dressing. 3.0 by 1.9. Slow.
She called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in early summer. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.

Week 4. 3.0 by 1.9, area 5.7 square centimeters, down from 6.4 at the start, about 11 percent reduction after 4 weeks of standard care with debridement, offloading, and moist dressings. Less than 50 percent; qualifies for a cellular tissue product. Sharp debridement today.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, she will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.

Application of a cellular tissue-based product to the left plantar forefoot ulcer after sharp debridement, 4 square centimeters, secured with a nonadherent dressing and the offloading boot. Weekly follow-up.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 50 denial can be answered from the record.
